correctness.rationale: For any sorted nonnegative integer vector h<=g. Total C<=8 forces g<=2, so no pair of (h,g) has strict opposite coordinate order. With C=9, n<=2 forces g<=2 while n=3 forces g=3 for every profile; hence n=4 is minimal. Exact integer partition enumeration at n=4,C=9 independently recovered 3 profiles with (h,g)=(1,3) and 5 with (2,2), giving 15 unordered reversing pairs. Positive four-paper C=9 has zero, C=10 has exactly (7,1,1,1) versus (4,2,2,2) and (3,3,2,2). Exhaustively checked no reversal for every n<=10,C<=8. Standard g definition caps at actual n; finite enumeration covers only the claimed first finite layers while universal lower bound is symbolic.
residual_risks: The g index has an uncapped alternative definition with padded fictitious papers; it is expressly not this claim.

value.rationale: The smallest possible reversal under jointly fixed publication count and citation sum is a natural precise robustness boundary for two established bibliometric measures. The 15-pair unrestricted layer and the separate strictly-positive publication variant quantify how concentration alone can change ordinal rankings, allowing reproducible minimum-complexity test cases. This is a complete motivated finite classification, not a random example and not a preference claim about which index better measures research quality.
residual_risks: Interpretation is mathematical and ordinal; not an empirical recommendation about researchers.

limitations: Same n and C required; g<=n definition; positive variant explicitly separate.
Results do not measure real researcher quality.
